I grew up in a strict South Asian household. My mother is an intense personality - definitely someone who resented being a mother. As much as she "loved" and "cared" for my sister and I, it was clear that if we weren't planning on becoming the people she had envisioned us to become, we wouldn't get any love. She has major anger issues, prone to violent outbursts at random times. I was always walking on egg shells because of this - I never really knew when it was going to happen. My parents fought a whole lot. Daily even. Loud, epic shouting matches I'd listen to from the top of the staircase. To this day I don't know if it was because my Mom has major issues, or because my Dad was always pissing her off by being neglectful. I'm probably in denial about a lot of things. As a kid, I would run down the stairs and try to calm things down - be the heroic mediator - but this rarely proved a successful strategy. You would think that the presence of a child would get to grown adults to calm their shit down, but it didn't. In fact, I would get caught in the cross-fire, often getting verbally beat up by mother in the process. My dad is an incredibly nice guy - albiet conservative. He also had a vision for who I was supposed to become. The difference between he and my mother is that my dad eventually saw that I was becoming my own person, and supported me. Where he failed was in never truly protecting me from my mothers verbal and emotional abuse - he continues to enable to this day saying things like, "underneath it all, she truly loves you. no one loves you more than her". Right. Oh, and I have an older sister. She's basically a carbon copy of my mother. I've always wished she'd be on my side, knowing how it is and all, but her loyalties are with my parents. She and have always been materially taken care of by our parents - but emotionally - we grew up in a severely codependant family. We're both damaged because of it.

Fast forward to today. I've been in a great relationship for nearly 4 years now, and married for almost 2. My wife is the joy I'd been waiting for my whole life. She loves the real me - not the facade I put up for the world. Not the guy my parents wanted me to be, but the guy I actually became. As you can imagine, visiting my parents, or having them visit me is DRAMA. Usually, the first day goes fine, no events. By the second day, all hell breaks loose. My mom starts critiquing everything, criticizing everything, complaining that we don't visit enough or that my wife doesn't talk enough. The truth is, while they've only selectively admitted to it, they aren't huge fans of my wife. I suppose this is because they expected me to marry differently, perhaps within our own culture. I didn't. In fact, I didn't get married the way I'm "supposed to", and didn't pick the job I was "supposed to", and I don't follow their imaginary rules. This has created resent and frustration on their side.

Long story short, the visits got taxing, so we got some therapy, and decided to create boundaries. I personally have no issue spending a few days, twice a year with my folks. I still love them despite everything that has happened, and I want to have a relationship. My wife knows this, and has made some efforts to do the same. After 4 years of trying she's had it. After a recent visit that went bad - meaning we had set healthy time boundaries before hand that angered my folks - I didn't do the best job maintaining the boundaries - my wife has decided that she needs to go NC. I'm devastated by this, because I just don't understand why we can't all just work this out. It's hard for me to imagine a life where I'm always visiting my parents alone. Or going on family vacations without my wife coming too. I'm holding onto some hope, but she seems pretty adamant. I'm starting to get pretty depressed about it all, and fear that this is going to tear our marriage apart. I feel like she's not really seeing the big picture. Staying LC would mean a lot to me, and our marriage.

I know it's not just about my feelings, her feelings are my priority as well. I just want her to feel safe, protected, and loved. What can I do to help her feel that LC can work for us? Whenever she feels like I am siding with my family, or being critical of her, she is quick to say NC is her game plan. But whenever she and I are really connecting, and being open and honest with each other, I see a glimmer of hope. She says, "you want me to go LC? are they ever going to change?" This is a fair point, I don't really believe they are going to change, but can't she and I change our mind-set and how we choose to respond to personalities that we don't necessarily always like?
